extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in Kunal Kamra / Indian stand-up and political satire
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article profiling Indian stand-up comedian and political satirist Kunal Kamra, describing his style, shows, notable episodes, controversies, and filmography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observational comedy about absurdities of life
rubrics_metrics.description: Kunal Kamra is known for his observational comedy about absurdities of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: performances include jokes about politics, cabbies, bachelor life and TV advertisements. (Original phrasing: 'His performances include jokes about politics, cabbies, bachelor life and TV advertisements.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of political satire in performances
rubrics_metrics.description: Kamra is a political satirist whose material frequently targets politics and public attitudes (e.g., a 2017 video 'Patriotism and the Government' mocking demonetization, the government and Indians' attitudes towards the army).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article documents real-world consequences of political satire: a 2017 clip led to death threats; airline bans and legal complaints followed later incidents. This indicates political satire may provoke backlash, bans, and legal/disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shut Up Ya Kunal — episode format
rubrics_metrics.description: The episodes typically feature a conversation with one or more invited guests, interposed with clips of news segments or debates, edited for humour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further detail: 'The show features Kamra engaged in an informal discussion with politicians and activists from both ends of the spectrum.' Ramit Verma is listed as the show's creative director and editor. First episode aired 20 July 2017. Use of conversational, informal interview plus edited clips is the stated format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of news/archival clips to create comedic contradiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Videos are interspersed with news clips of the guests contradicting their own statements to comic effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: juxtapose a guest's current remarks with prior news footage/debates that show contradictions; editing is used 'for humour' to highlight hypocrisy or inconsistency. (Original phrasing: 'The videos are interspersed with news clips of the guests contradicting their own statements to comic effect.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Guest selection spanning political spectrum
rubrics_metrics.description: The show invites politicians, activists, journalists and public figures from both ends of the political spectrum as guests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from episode list: guests include representatives from BJP, Congress, Aam Aadmi Party, commentators, activists and journalists (e.g., Madhukeshwar Desai, Priyanka Chaturvedi, Kanhaiya Kumar, Ravish Kumar, Asaduddin Owaisi, Arvind Kejriwal). The page implies deliberate cross-spectrum guest selection to foster debate and comedic tension.
